newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Electrabel near compromise on supply contracts.
newsitem.headline: EU, Electrabel near compromise on supply contracts.

text.p: The European Commission and Electrabel are nearing an agreement that would allow the Belgian electricity company to be the sole supplier of the country's municipalities for a period of 10 years only.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told reporters that the supply contracts could last up to 15 years but "after 10 years the exclusivity should be ended and the Intercommunales should already be able to buy a maximum 25 percent (of their electricity needs) elsewhere".

Electrabel had initially offered the Belgian Intercommunales -- joint ventures between municipalities for the distribution of electricity -- to sign up for 30-year exclusive supply contracts. In return, they could buy a stake in Electrabel.
Van Miert was speaking after he addressed a meeting of the Belgian Federation of Enterprises FEB/VBO on the Commission's view on competition policy and public aids.

A Commission source close to Van Miert said earlier on Tuesday that Electrabel and the Intercommunales must still give their formal assent to the agreement before it can be submitted to the Commission for approval.
A final decision could be reached before the end of the month, the source said.
